security_audit.summary: Most static external-command detections are Markdown fence or inline-code false positives. Several bash examples do document npx claude-flow commands, which can execute external npm package code if an agent runs them automatically. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, obfuscation, or malicious network behavior was found.

remediation.issue: Unpinned npx command examples can execute code from an external package source.
remediation.suggestion: Pin claude-flow to a reviewed version in every npx example, or require a trusted local installation before use.

remediation.issue: The skill contains many runnable shell examples that could be followed automatically by an agent.
remediation.suggestion: State that agents must ask for user confirmation before running shell commands, especially commands that change sessions or memory.

remediation.issue: Maintenance examples include memory export and clear operations.
remediation.suggestion: Add backup and restore guidance before destructive memory maintenance commands are run.

content.value_statement: Complex AI projects need clear coordination across many agents. This skill guides Claude Flow hive mind workflows with queens, workers, consensus, sessions, and memory.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to initialize Claude Flow hive mind projects.
Shows how to spawn queen-led swarms with worker limits and objectives.
Describes majority, weighted, and Byzantine consensus modes.
Covers session pause, resume, stop, export, and import workflows.
Documents collective memory storage, search, association, and optimization patterns.
Connects hive mind workflows with SPARC, GitHub review, and Claude Code task generation.
limitations: Provides documentation and workflow guidance, not a standalone agent runtime.
Requires Claude Flow or compatible tooling to run the shown commands.
Command examples may change local session or memory state when executed.
Consensus quality depends on worker prompts, available context, and user review.

use_cases.title: Plan a Large Engineering Build
use_cases.description: Use a strategic queen to divide architecture, implementation, testing, and documentation across specialized agents.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Pull Request Review
use_cases.description: Spawn reviewer, security, performance, and test agents, then use consensus to decide required changes.

use_cases.title: Preserve Project Knowledge
use_cases.description: Store decisions, results, and recurring patterns in collective memory for later sessions.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Hive
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hive mind advanced skill to initialize a basic Claude Flow hive for my project. Explain each command before running anything.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Queen and Consensus
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose a queen type and consensus algorithm for this objective: [objective]. Include worker roles and risks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Session Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a hive mind session plan for [project]. Include checkpoints, memory entries, status checks, and review gates.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Multi-Hive Program
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an advanced multi-hive workflow for [program]. Include shared memory, scaling rules, consensus thresholds, and failure recovery.

output_examples.input: Plan a hive for building an authentication service.
output_examples.output: A strategic queen coordinates architecture, backend, database, security, test, and documentation workers with weighted consensus for key design choices.

output_examples.input: Review a pull request with multiple concerns.
output: A tactical queen assigns code quality, security, performance, and test coverage reviews.
The hive records findings in memory and reaches consensus on required changes.

output_examples.input: Improve slow task assignment in an existing hive.
output_examples.output: The workflow checks queue metrics, worker load, cache behavior, and memory usage before recommending scaling changes.

best_practices: Review every shell command before execution and confirm the package source.
Use strategic queens for planning and tactical queens for implementation-heavy work.
Store important decisions and results in collective memory with clear labels.
anti_patterns: Do not run unreviewed npx commands from a community skill without confirmation.
Do not use Byzantine consensus for simple low-risk decisions.
Do not spawn more workers than the task context and review process can support.

faq.question: What does this skill help coordinate?
faq.answer: It helps coordinate Claude Flow hive mind workflows with queen agents, worker roles, consensus, sessions, and collective memory.

faq.question: Does this skill include executable code?
faq.answer: The skill is a Markdown guide. It includes shell examples that can run external commands if a user or agent executes them.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: When should I use Byzantine consensus?
faq.answer: Use it for important decisions that need stronger agreement, such as architecture choices or release readiness.

faq.question: Can this skill manage long-running work?
faq.answer: It documents session workflows for pause, resume, checkpoints, status checks, export, and import.

faq.question: What should I review before publishing this skill?
faq.answer: Review all npx examples, pin trusted package versions, and require confirmation before commands change local state.
